messages:
maria (Design): dropping the latest key-management modal v3 mock here. main asks: 1) should rotate keep the user in the modal so they can copy the secret, or send them back to the list? 2) wording for revoke needs to be clearer for non-devs. thoughts? josh (Engineering): technically we can keep them in the modal and auto-select the revealed secret in the field. current flow routes to list on success, but it's easy to change. only concern is focus/announcements for screen readers. liam (A11y): strongly prefer staying in-modal. If we navigate out, many SR users lose anchor and have to find the list again. If we stay, make sure the new secret area is announced and selected. Also the revoke copy needs an assertive announcement. nina (PM): product prefers getting people back to list so they can see other keys, but copying the new secret is higher priority. compromise: stay in-modal, show a clear primary CTA "Done, return to keys" and also show an inline helper "Copy now — you'll only see this once" next to the secret. maria (Design): updated copy suggestion for revoke panel: "Revoking this key will immediately stop any services using it. This action is permanent and cannot be undone." Also increased icon contrast and added a stronger border. josh (Engineering): implementation note: to announce the revoke warning, we can add role=\"alert\" or aria-live=\"assertive\" on the message. be careful to not accidentally announce the whole modal twice when focus changes. liam (A11y): code snippet suggestion for the warning:
Revoking this key will immediately stop any services using it. This action is permanent and cannot be undone.
. Also recommend tooltip/description for the role dropdown — a lot of folks default to "Admin" without understanding implications. Tooltip must be keyboard accessible and triggered via an info button, not hover only. maria (Design): putting a small info button next to the Role dropdown that opens a persistent tooltip panel. microcopy: "Admin: can create, rotate, and revoke keys. Read/Write: can use the key. Read: read-only token access." trying to keep it short. nina (PM): also add an inline guardrail when someone selects Admin: lightweight confirmation check: a line that says "Are you sure? Admin keys can manage apps." with a secondary checkbox maybe? or do we avoid extra friction? josh (Engineering): checkbox is extra complexity but doable. prefer a subtle inline confirmation rather than a modal confirmation to avoid modal-stack fatigue. e.g., show a yellow banner under the dropdown: "Admin grants full access — double-check this role." with a link to docs. liam (A11y): ensure the inline banner is programmatically connected (aria-describedby) so assistive tech reads it when role changes. Also ensure color is not the only cue; add icon + text. Contrast >= 4.5:1 for the icon/text block. maria (Design): agreed. i'll update mocks to: stay in-modal after rotate, auto-select secret field + show "Copy now — expires on close" helper, add accessible assertive revoke warning, info button for Role with keyboard target, and inline banner when Admin selected. will push an updated figma and copy PR later today. :sparkles: ci-bot: pipeline passed for branch feature/keys-v3-accessibility (build 2026-10-02T14:22Z). nina (PM): thanks all. can we do a quick 10-minute pairing once the PR is up to verify focus order for keyboard and SR? I'll ping again when ready. josh (Engineering): happy to pair. liam (A11y): I'll join and run through the checklist (announce, focus, tooltip accessibility, color contrast).
